mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 drops and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (more than 0.5% in a month) signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power diminishes.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (more than 1% month-over-month) signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) also increases, it signals a strengthening demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% MoM and RSAFS increase
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST, RSAFS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as immediate economic concerns arise.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between FEDFUNDS, CPIAUCSL conditions and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
